Steer clear of this store if you expect professional customer service.

We bought an expensive ring here and were offered a size adjustment through the store since the correct size was not available. When purchasing, we were informed that this would take approximately 2-4 weeks.

Instead, the entire process took almost 7 weeks.

Throughout the entire period, we only received vague explanations and new delays every time we contacted them. Afterwards, the store suddenly started claiming that the delivery time was actually 4-6 weeks, which does not match what we were informed when purchasing.

When the ring finally returned, we discovered at home upon closer inspection that it had visible marks, scratches and an uneven finish that were not there before the adjustment.

What also felt very unprofessional was how the ring was handled in the store. The employee tried the ring on his own finger in front of us before it was sent in for adjustment. When the ring was later returned, the original marking was gone, and the ring came back in a simple plastic bag with a note before being put back in the box.

The most frustrating thing has been the handling afterwards.

Instead of taking responsibility, we experienced a lack of follow-up, changing explanations, a sharp tone in communication and finally complete ignoring for several weeks.

The store itself suggested sending it to the head office as a solution. I accepted this immediately, but then received no further follow-up or response.

It is honestly difficult to understand how a store that sells expensive jewelry can think that this is acceptable customer treatment.

Waiting almost 7 weeks to then get the ring back in worse condition, and then being ignored, is simply not fair.

The case has been forwarded to the Consumer Council.

Cannot be recommended.

one_star_reviews.text:
My daughter bought a stroller via Klarna. After nine months of normal use, the stroller was broken.

We first contacted the seller, but the seller has since stopped selling strollers and has not cleaned up, despite repeated promises to get back to us. When the seller did not follow up, we chose to complain to Klarna with reference to the Financial Contracts Act, Section 2-7, first paragraph.

It turned out to be almost as demanding as the dialogue with the seller.

The complaint to Klarna had to be handled in English and via chat. When we tried to upload documentation, the chat was closed due to inactivity. Klarna then referred to its internal complaint deadline of 180 days, and our experience is that they did not take a position on the rights the customer has under Norwegian consumer law and the Financial Contracts Act.

After much back and forth with the customer service representative, the case was finally registered with a reference number. My daughter was told that she would be kept updated.

After 11 days she still hadn't heard anything, so we contacted Klarna to get the status. We were then told that the case had been closed and concluded — without us being informed, without justification, and without us being able to see that Klarna had actually handled the case.

The next step is therefore the Financial Complaints Board.

Two clear pieces of advice from us:

Do not buy a Bellino stroller.

And don't assume that Klarna will automatically give you the security you might think you have if something goes wrong after the purchase. In any case, our experience has been that it has been very difficult to get Klarna to deal with the case in an orderly manner.

one_star_reviews.text: At first, this seemed like a fantastic clinic. However, it turned out that they lack knowledge in a number of areas. They referred me to Bergen Small Animal Clinic (Leif) because of my little chihuahua's knee. At that time, they had x-rayed the back and hips, but forgot to x-ray the elbows, even though my dog ​​showed signs of pain there too. I was told that the dog had a hip defect, which could not be done. When it came to the dog's behavioral changes, I was told to contact a behavior specialist. If it hadn't been for the fact that she had injured her knee, I would not have found out that the dog was missing a vertebra, which caused her to have a lot of pain there. They had forgotten to check the x-rays on the back, and I was told by them that it was because there were so many other things with the dog. The dog also had an open fontanel, and when Leif at the small animal clinic used an ultrasound on the brain, it turned out that only about half of the brain was as it should be. This could therefore be the reason for her behavioral changes. If the hip had been her only problem, Leif could have easily operated on her. So misinformation from Fanafjorden, when they said there was nothing to be done. With all the things together, it was a big surprise for me that euthanasia would be the best thing for my two-year-old chihuhua. According to Fanafjorden, they thought that Leif could fix the knee, a behavior specialist could help with the behavior and she could get painkillers for the hip. The knee was the least of the problems, and according to Leif, it could fix itself. I also received word from Fanafjorden when I emailed them after visiting Leif that they had discussed the shape of the dog's head, but this without telling me anything. So they can be kind and straightforward with my dog, but considering the lack of knowledge and communication, I would never take my new dog to them again. Lost all trust in them, unfortunately since I had heard so many good things about them before my meeting with them. Unfortunately, this is an experience we cannot recommend.
The dialogue was good in advance, but the photographer demanded full payment 14 days before the wedding. This turned out to be a big mistake on our part to accept, as we were practically left with no means of pressure whatsoever when the delivery did not meet expectations.

A new round of editing was done, but unfortunately the result was no better – quite the opposite.
After much back and forth, we were promised a memory box as compensation. We still have not received this.
We also asked for financial compensation and access to the raw material due to the dissatisfaction, but this was refused.
All in all, we are left with some usable images, but a large majority that in our opinion do not meet the expected standard. Our experience has been characterized by a lack of follow-up and a result that did not correspond to what we experienced as having been predicted.

one_star_reviews.text: Bad customer service. Rude.

I have been buying garden equipment from Eik Motorsenter in Rykene for several years, including Husqvarna robotic mowers, and that is precisely why this review is extra difficult to write.

The price and service at the time of sale were good, and have been pleasant in meetings. The problem is the technical craftsmanship, follow-up and disclaimer of liability over time.

I bought a Husqvarna robotic mower in the fall of 2021, which was recommended by the dealer for my plot (approx. 900 m² + extensions). They themselves were responsible for the complete installation with cable. From the first season, the mower has had persistent problems: false cable breaks, loss of loop signal, transponder errors and repeated messages about a blocked charging station without there actually being any blockage.

The problems have been so extensive that the dealer itself has stated that they have never had a customer with so many errors. Nevertheless, the solution has largely been to explain everything as "cable", despite the fact that the cable has been laid by them and that all cable runs have been checked with a multimeter, test loops and Husqvarna's own troubleshooting methods - without actual breaks or abnormal values.
The mower was at one point almost completely dismantled and large parts of the innards replaced. There was also talk of a full replacement, which was postponed and postponed until the machine was finally replaced, but the charging station and cable layout were retained, and the problems continued again after a while, which made the situation essentially unchanged.
I have spent hundreds of hours over several seasons on troubleshooting, cable replacement, transport to the workshop and manual mowing of a lawn of over one acre - precisely what the robot was supposed to eliminate. The mower has less than 900 operating hours after several years, which in itself documents that the solution has never worked as intended.
In the end, I was left with an unstable robot that "works in the workshop", but not in practice. When the complaint/goodwill was raised based on history and documentation, this was rejected – despite the fact that the problems had been reported right from the start. At one point they considered giving me a new machine, since they had never experienced a customer who had so many problems, but if they did, I was told not to shop with them again!
Conclusion: Nice people, but when advanced technical equipment does not work over time, and responsibility is pulverized between cable, software and customer, you are left alone. I recommend thinking carefully about where you buy a robotic lawnmower if you expect real follow-up when there are actually challenges. The case has been sent to the Consumer Council, but they have a long processing time and Eik Motorsenter probably knows that - I think I'm going to give up, but I have over 50 emails, pictures and formal complaints. Too bad they couldn't sort it out when they themselves have confirmed that something is wrong and has been wrong, before reporting and submitting the case to the Consumer Council.

I reached out to Helmr as I thought they might help me with my current work situation I'm facing. While they seemed fairly knowledgeable they were things they did not know that I inquired about regarding Norwegian labor laws. They seemed disappointed to hear that I didn't want to make things ugly with my current employer regarding unpaid OT. Shortly after discussing this via video call, they decided to drop my case.

Afterwards I was sent an invoice that seemed to wayyyyyyyyy more than it should be for the amount of work I received. I know that lawyers are expensive, but this seems excessive.

Aside from the preliminary exchange of basic information, a 1 hour video conference call and a follow up email. I was billed for 30,000 NOK!!!! I feel they've done this out of spite, and they're trying to take advantage of my unfamiliarity with Norway in general as a disabled American skilled labor immigrant.

After receiving the invoice I sent an email requesting a further breakdown of what and how I was billed as there does not appear to be anything specific about how I was charged. As of writing this review they have not responded.

I did file a formal complaint with the  Advokatklageordningen, as I feel this invoice is extortive and lacking specifics on how I was charged. All that being said, the woman who was assigned to assist with my case was quite helpful.

I visited Pust for the first time. The location is beautiful and the waterfront setting is definitely a highlight. Unfortunately, my experience was negatively affected by what I consider a serious security issue.

The men’s changing room appeared to be intended as a restricted area, accessible only by code. However, a hose for the cold plunge buckets was running through the doorway, preventing the door from closing properly. As a result, the changing room remained partially open during the session.

After about 30 minutes, several people who were not part of our sauna session climbed over the entrance barrier and entered the changing room area. They were only inside briefly, and once I started paying close attention to what they were doing, they left almost immediately. This gave me the impression that they were not actually supposed to be there, which made me concerned about the security of the facility and uncomfortable about leaving my belongings unattended.

Instead of relaxing and enjoying the sauna, I spent a significant amount of time monitoring my personal items. A sauna visit should feel safe and secure, not stressful.

Management should address this issue immediately. If access to changing rooms is supposed to be restricted, the doors should be able to close and lock properly. Otherwise, anyone nearby can potentially enter areas that are intended for paying guests.

one_star_reviews.text: Apgaus

If you love your car, I would be EXTREMELY careful about delivering the car to Toyota Økern without full documentation before handing it in.

I handed my car in for service and got it back with new damage to the rims. Not old marks, but fresh wounds/scratches that I discovered immediately after handing it in. I went back just minutes later to report it, but was met with the standard phrase: “This was there before” and that I had probably “drove on the curb”.

The most provocative thing was hardly the damage, but the attitude. I was actually told that I “should have taken pictures of the car before handing it in”. So there you have it, basically, the summary of how such cases are handled here: If you have not documented absolutely everything yourself in advance, you are on your own and will most likely be blamed.

And this comes from a workshop that previously managed to install my taillight incorrectly after repair. The taillight was above the molding by the rear window on one side, while the other side clearly showed how it was actually supposed to be installed. No quality control. No follow-up. I dismantled and fixed the job myself at home in the garage as it felt safer than handing the car in again.

It is quite incredible that you hand in the car to a branded workshop and end up having to check and repair it yourself.

The premises look nice and modern in front of the customers, but what actually happens in the back of the workshop is clearly a completely different story.

My honest advice:

- Take detailed photos of ALL rims, bodywork and interior before handing it in.
- Film the car around before handing over the keys.
- Require documentation of work carried out.
- Carefully inspect the car BEFORE you drive away.

Otherwise you risk that any damage will simply be rejected, and that the blame will automatically be placed on you as the customer.

Just steer clear of the place.

I have previously been a customer of Oslo Laserklinikk for laser hair removal on the body and face, but chose to change clinics due to the poor eye safety during the treatments. People considering laser hair removal at Oslo Laserklinikk should be particularly aware of this.

As a doctor, I reacted strongly to the eye protection used during laser treatment on the face. When treating close to the eyes, stable metal shields should be standard, not laser glasses that provide poorer coverage.

The metal shields that were used had no attachment device and therefore did not sit stably enough. The laser glasses also did not provide good enough coverage from the sides and from above. When the treatment is carried out close to the eyes, the clinic should use robust metal shields that actually sit securely.

During laser hair removal, especially in the facial area, powerful laser energy is used very close to the eyes. Therefore, the eye protection must sit completely stable and tight to provide the best possible coverage throughout the treatment. Inadequate eye protection when using medical lasers can, in the worst case, lead to serious eye damage and permanent vision loss.

After changing laser clinics, I have experienced eye protection that appears significantly better and more professional. The contrast was so great that it reinforced the impression that eye safety at Oslo Laserklinikk was not taken seriously enough.

I bought a house last year and discovered a water leak in the soffit (cornice). I went up on the roof to check and stepped through the roof and hit the gutter, which meant I had to get 8 stitches in my shin. There were several gaps between the roof tile and the gutter fitting, and it turns out that the previous owner had not maintained the roof and checked that the roof tile covered the gutter. The water had seeped in under the gutter and along the battens and roof trusses, which had caused it to rot along the stretch from the gutter to the gutter. I contacted Help for help with change of ownership insurance, where I attached several photos for documentation. Then I got a response from Kristine Andersen Tytingvåg that the roof was more than half of what was expected and that they were only following the legal requirements. That's it!
I have now replaced all of the battens, soffit/sheeting, but the roof tile that this lawyer thought was unusable is still on the roof, and now the roof is sealed.

If you get Kristine Andersen Tytingvåg, please ask for another case manager, because this lady is completely useless!!! Do not choose home purchase insurance via Help!!!

Going to a restaurant is about much more than just the food. The atmosphere, the service and how you are treated as a paying guest are at least as important. In a service industry, customer satisfaction is crucial. A few unhappy customers may be ignored in the short term, but over time, such an attitude will damage the place.

I used to visit this restaurant before it burned down, and was consistently very satisfied. Therefore, I was looking forward to returning after the renovation and recreating the good experience I had previously had there. We visited the restaurant (Terrassen) on Friday, May 22.

Unfortunately, the evening was the exact opposite of what we had hoped for. Right at the entrance, we were greeted by a waiter with an arrogant, condescending and downright unpleasant demeanor. He was a heavily built man, about 35 to 40 years old, dark-haired and Swedish-speaking. His entire appearance was characterized by irritation, complacency and a lack of respect for the guests. From the very beginning it seemed as if he actively wanted to make the experience as uncomfortable as possible.

It is actually impressive how effectively one employee can ruin the mood of an entire restaurant visit. What was supposed to be a pleasant evening ended up being an unpleasant experience that we sincerely regret. We now unfortunately associate this restaurant with poor treatment and a very creepy atmosphere.

We will not be returning, nor can we recommend others to go there.

one_star_reviews.text:
I am writing this to warn others, based on my personal experience with a former PT at SATS Vågsbygd. Others may have had different experiences, but this is mine.

I was in a mentally vulnerable period and was seeking help, not just training. I first met the trainer through a free public youth service, where trust was built in a helping role. Eventually, I experienced that the path forward was shifted to a private and paid client relationship. I said yes because I trusted him.

In my experience, the relationship eventually became very asymmetrical. I experienced extreme pressure, harsh personal comments and a form of follow-up that went far beyond normal personal training. Criticism was directed at me as a person, not just towards training or effort. I experienced the language used as degrading and mentally stressful.

The collaboration eventually became about more than training. PT classes were used for conversations about work, finances, private life and personal problems. I did not experience that there were clear boundaries between commercial PT follow-up, personal support and influence on life choices.

The training and diet program was also experienced as extreme. I felt pressured to gain weight quickly, eat large amounts of food and do hard sessions, even when this became mentally and physically stressful. I also experienced that further cooperation could be made dependent on me reaching certain goals in a short time.

Financially, this was very stressful. I paid a total of around 274,000 NOK. In my experience, there were unclear frameworks, inadequate contract understanding and weak documentation about how the follow-up actually took place. I also experienced that many PT clips were pulled together over a short period of time.

I believe that SATS should have much better control over how PTs follow up vulnerable clients, especially when the relationship develops into one about psychological support, finances, work, private life and dependence on the trainer. It should not be possible for a commercial PT relationship to have such great influence without clear boundaries, documentation and responsibility.

When I later raised the issue and demanded a refund, I experienced that the responsibility was largely shifted away from the center and onto the individual trainer. For me, this shows a serious problem: If the center makes money from the PT services, the center should also have real insight into and responsibility for how the services are delivered.

I have tried to share my experience publicly, but now also experience that my criticism is stopped, limited or attempted to be removed. To me, this appears as censorship of a real customer experience. It makes the case even more serious, because this is about consumers' right to warn others when they believe a service has been harmful, unprofessional or irresponsible.

The consequences for me have been very serious. I have spent an enormous amount of time processing the relationship and the experiences afterwards. I have documentation of much of what I describe, and the case is not closed.

My advice to others is to be very careful about mixing personal training, mental vulnerability, financial pressure and private support. A PT is not the same as an authorized healthcare professional. Fitness chains operate commercially, and as a customer you can be left with great risk if the boundaries become blurred.

Today I went here with a close friend. We are the same age and behave according to the rules. Inside the park there is a foam pool that everyone knows about. As many people know, it takes quite a long time to get out of there – it is very difficult to get back up.

My friend and I wanted to jump down from a height. First I jumped, in the middle of the pool, and then my friend jumped. But before she jumped, I was already trying to get out. I was struggling a lot, my socks were falling off all the time, and I could hardly move. After my friend jumped, I first tried to help her out so that she could help me up later. At the same time, we laughed a little at the situation because it was difficult to get out.

Suddenly, a female employee came from behind, probably about 17-18 years old. She behaved very arrogantly. She treated me incredibly rudely, even though she could clearly see that I was struggling to get up. In a loud and irritated voice she said:
“GET OUT. YOU JUMPED, DONE.”

She said it in an angry and commanding way. You are an employee, so you should be aware of both your tone and your behavior. I had no bad intentions at all. We were just laughing because I actually couldn’t get out of there. But suddenly she spoke to me as if she was giving orders to a dog. Very disrespectful and inappropriate.

I became very uncomfortable because of this employee, and I will not go back there again. I don’t want to be in a place where employees treat customers this way. After she spoke to me like that, all desire to have fun disappeared, and we left the park before our time was up. Besides, there was no one else to jump from the spot we jumped from. I am so glad I did not buy this subscription. In my opinion, the price is unreasonably high, and it seems like an agreement that will be very expensive for the residents in practice. Of the almost 80 charging points in the housing association, all are unused, which says something about how unattractive the solution is.

Unfortunately, our housing association has entered into a bad agreement, and with this I also want to warn others against falling into the same trap. When you look at the terribly expensive agreement in the picture, it is difficult to recommend this further. This appears to be not very user-friendly and not worth the money.

Steer clear if you can. Aneo Mobility establishes itself as a charging monopoly in housing associations and condominiums, and then reserves the right to change the pricing model and terms at its own discretion. This is a lousy deal for consumers, who will be locked into this one home charging provider for the foreseeable future. The only way to escape is to move.

When home charging ends up costing as much as or more per kWh than fast charging, then something is terribly, terribly wrong. The information that was sent out in connection with the transition from charging packages with a fixed price, to a spot price plus a fixed monthly fee, was in practice a pure cover-up of the fact that the new pricing model was going to be considerably more expensive for many customers. This insincerity in combination with sky-high charging prices means that I really can't recommend this company enough.

Visit to Becks Brasserie, Drammen – May 29, 2026 Unfortunately, I have to say that this was one of the weakest restaurant experiences we have had in a long time. We had been looking forward to celebrating our wedding anniversary with good food, wine and a pleasant evening out, but unfortunately went home disappointed. We were greeted by a very nice lady who showed us to our table. She made a good first impression and did her job in a professional manner. Then the waiter who was supposed to accompany us throughout the evening took over. He seemed uninterested in service from the start and seemed most interested in getting our order taken as quickly as possible. We were honestly unsure whether he was a waiter or had another role in the restaurant, as he did not seem particularly engaged with the guests. The drinks were eventually placed on the table without any particular follow-up or sense of hospitality. Some dry waiting bread with aioli was served. The food arrived within a reasonable time. We ordered a FILÉT DON FRANCISCO and a BECKS Steak (tenderloin). The FILÉT DON FRANCISCO steaks had different degrees of doneness. One was medium+, while the other was well done. The taste was good, however. The side dish was a bit soggy cauliflower. My wife's Beck's Steak was ordered medium, but came out almost well done. It was a little pink in the middle if you put it in the goodwill, but the meat was also hard-cooked on the outside and contained several hard parts that had to be spit out. The fries were dry and boring, the side dish tasted good. When we pointed this out to the waiter, we unfortunately did not feel taken seriously. He initially dismissed the objection and asked my wife to cut the steak in half. After seeing that it had some pink in the center, he thought it was medium or maybe medium+. Body language and facial expression also gave the clear impression that he thought the complaint was unnecessary. He finally offered to have a new steak made, but by then the situation had already become uncomfortable, and my wife did not want to sit alone and wait for new food while I finished mine. After we finished eating, it was about 30 minutes before we saw the waiter again. When he came to clear the table, he dropped and broke a glass right next to me. Accidents can happen, of course, but what surprised us was that he neither apologized for the incident nor asked if everything was okay. He eventually came with the dustpan and picked up the broken glass. Furthermore, we were not asked if we wanted more drinks or dessert. The waiter was simply absent for much of the evening. It was only about ten minutes after clearing that we got attention again, and then we had to ask for the dessert menu ourselves. We ended up going to the bar to pay, not with our waiter but with the lady who greeted us. What makes this experience extra disappointing is that this was not our first visit to Becks. We have visited Becks several times before, both in Drammen, Larvik and Skien, and have always been very satisfied with both the food and the service. We have also celebrated our wedding anniversary at Becks on two previous occasions, with very good experiences both times. That is precisely why we had high expectations this time. We chose Becks because we had good experiences before and wanted to celebrate the day in a place we trusted. Unfortunately, this evening was so disappointing that we are left with the feeling that we do not want to return. It is sad to say about a restaurant that we have previously recommended and visited with pleasure. We understand that everyone can have a bad day, and that both the kitchen and the service can experience challenges, but it was not particularly full or busy as it appeared. However, when both the dining experience, the handling of a feedback on the meat and the general service fail on the same evening, the overall impression is unfortunately very negative. We hope this feedback is taken as constructive criticism, because Becks has previously shown us that they can deliver far better than this.

Based on this, I decided to give the clinic another chance. This meant that I had to set aside a significant amount of time over two days, including taking time off work, which also resulted in a financial loss for me.

Instead of a factual and professional follow-up, I was later contacted directly by the dentist in question. The conversation was experienced as unpleasant and unprofessional, characterized by a confrontational tone and a lack of understanding that I, as a patient, had expressed dissatisfaction with the treatment and handling of the situation. It also appeared problematic that the person the complaint concerned handled the complaint himself, without any form of neutral or professional follow-up from management.

Overall, I am left with an impression of inadequate communication, poor patient management and a lack of professionalism in the face of legitimate feedback. I am sharing this experience because I believe it is important that other patients get a more nuanced picture before choosing the clinic.

Ordered a shed with accessories from Grønt Fokus, but this unfortunately developed into a very bad buying experience.

First, there were ambiguities around the product description of the gutter/fitting package, where the description was misleading in my opinion. Even Grønt Fokus later admitted that the text should be changed.

The communication from the complaints department was experienced as not very solution-oriented. I had to constantly remind myself about the status, and mostly just got told that they were waiting for the manufacturer. In the end, the compensation was offered as a price discount of 2%, which I think is very poor in relation to the inconveniences and delay.

one_star_reviews.text:
Waiting time in the hospital teaches a man two things: patience and that whoever controls the coffee machine actually controls the entire empire. I came here as a simple patient and will soon leave here as an old strategist with a lower back and life wisdom. Hercules would never have survived the waiting room without a neck massage and a thermos.

Sørlandet Hospital took this to heart and decided to go to war with my wrist.

First, the cast was so loose that it could have functioned as a toy for a giraffe (white). Second, it was so tight that the bloodstream sent a letter of resignation (red). Third, it was some kind of avant-garde art installation that no one understood (blue). Fourth? By then I had developed Stockholm syndrome and started thanking them for not amputating my arm. (White). They say I should cut the cast and leave it as it is, then they say I can change it at any time. Then they say I have to keep it on.

And the economy? There they are true Renaissance masters. They take your money with the grace of a Venetian tax collector, but if you complain about the treatment you get about the same response as a peasant asking the king for a tax refund in 1498.

First they send you to one clinic. There they look at you like you’re some medieval mystery before saying, “Hmm… another department must take this.” Then you’re sent on like an untracked parcel. The next clinic points you to a third, the third to a fourth, and suddenly you’ve traveled more around the system than Marco Polo.

I went in with a broken arm and came out an economic refugee. The most impressive thing is the efficiency: no one can agree on whether the cast should be loose or tight,

But the highlight was the X-rays. Four images. FOUR. At this point, I’m pretty sure my skeleton is now in better resolution than Google Earth. Every time they took a new picture it felt like a DLC purchase in a video game: “Want to see your wrist from a slightly different angle? It'll be an extra 400 kroner. I recommend researching the hospital before you go in. Over 2 thousand kroner for a hand is absurd.

This isn't a hospital; they never do anything. The so-called professionals who treated me were nothing but mediocre. They discharged me from the hospital while I was still experiencing multiple hemorrhages and was on the verge of fainting. And they were so cynical as to tell me it was "normal" and treat me like I was stupid.
Besides, they give you different treatment if you're a migrant.

I was in the emergency department with a fracture in my right wrist, and they ended up destroying all the fingers on my hand because of the first cast they put on. Later I had several meetings with them, but you'd be hard pressed to find more apathetic doctors. I came in with two fractures, and ended up with broken fingers on both hands. I've filed a complaint with them.

one_star_reviews.text: Organization that is supposed to fight racism, but it is a waste to contact them, they support visible racism and have little understanding of what racism really is. You are told that you have to fix this yourself, quite disappointing that such an organization cannot help achieve justice and fight racism.

In my view, the Antiracist Center does not appear as a neutral and principled actor against racism, but as an ideological organization with a clear double standard in how racism is discussed and assessed.
They seem to treat racism differently depending on who is affected. When minorities are exposed to incitement, generalizations or derogatory remarks, this is often referred to as serious racism, structural discrimination or hate speech. When similar generalizations, hostile language or condescending attitudes are directed at white Norwegians or other white majority groups, it often seems as if this is trivialized, explained away or framed as legitimate social criticism.
This creates the impression that the Antiracist Center is not primarily fighting against racism as a universal principle, but against one specific group position in society. White majority groups are often referred to through concepts such as power, privilege, whiteness and structures, while minority groups are to a much greater extent referred to as vulnerable and worthy of protection. The result is that the same type of language can be assessed completely differently depending on who it is directed at.
To me, this appears as a device that contributes to weakening, delegitimizing and undermining the legitimate place and voice of white majority groups in their own country. When a group is constantly portrayed as collectively guilty, privileged or morally suspect, while at the same time incitement against the same group is not met with the same seriousness, it is difficult to see this as real anti-racism.
Real anti-racism should be consistent. It should protect individuals and groups against racism regardless of skin color, ethnicity, religion, origin or majority status. If the Anti-Racist Center wants credibility, they should be clear that racism is unacceptable in all directions — even when it affects white Norwegians or other majority groups.
As long as this is not practiced consistently, their work is perceived as selective, ideological and unprincipled, and in my view it contributes more to polarization, distrust and ethnic conflict than to unity and real equality.

I have used this workshop for many years and have previously been satisfied. However, our recent experiences have been so serious that trust is now completely gone.

The most serious concerns a car where we explicitly – in writing – requested:

* price estimates for work and parts for known defects
* EU inspection
* an overall assessment of total costs before we decided on further work

This was important because the car has limited value, and if the total cost was too high, we would rather sell it.

What the workshop did was to completely ignore this.

After several weeks of no follow-up, we had to make a reminder ourselves. Then we were told that they had carried out the work we asked for a price for — but that they had “forgotten” the EU inspection. In other words, the part that would provide the basis for whether we even wanted to spend money on the car further.

The result was that we were initially left with a bill of almost 17,000 kroner, before we were later told that an additional 26,000 kroner would have to be spent to get the car EU-approved. A total of over 40,000 kroner.

If we had been given that information in advance — as we expressly requested — the car would never have been repaired. It would have been sold.

The most shocking thing is not only the fault itself, but how the workshop handles it afterwards. When we present written messages and documentation showing what was actually agreed, we only meet with evasion and silence. I recommend that everyone be extremely careful with written agreements, prices and approvals before work is carried out here.

SCAM WARNING: Hidden Subscription Trap (Abofalle) – Norwegian Health / L&L Pharma
​Review Text:
I am writing this to warn international customers about the deceptive business practices of Norwegian Health, Norwegian Lab, and L&L Pharma GmbH.
​The Scheme:
They lure customers with "cheap trial offers" or "free samples" for shipping costs only (approx. €5-€9). However, by completing the order, you are unknowingly enrolled in an expensive monthly subscription costing €50–€80 per month without clear consent.
​Legal Facts:
​Violation of German Law (§ 312j BGB): Under German law (the "Button Solution"), a contract is only valid if the "Buy" button clearly states that it leads to a recurring payment. These companies fail to provide this transparency.
​Legal Precedent: In April 2025, the Consumer Advice Center (Verbraucherzentrale Baden-Württemberg) successfully took legal action against Norwegian Lab AS (Case No. 13 O 67/24 KfH) for misleading consumers and violating the Button Solution.
​Unfair Terms: They often ignore withdrawal requests (Widerruf) and use aggressive tactics to collect money.

We visited a private pediatrician at Volvat after an urgent referral from our GP to Ahus due to our child's symptoms, based on family history. We needed a quick assessment while we waited for further follow-up. We also noticed that the pediatrician had experience from Ahus, which gave us an expectation of a safe and thorough assessment.

The experience towards the end of the consultation was very bad. The conversation seemed informal to us, and we were not informed that what was discussed would be included in the medical record. When we later read the medical record, we therefore reacted to its content.

Towards the end of the consultation, as we were about to finish and leave, the doctor addressed our concerns as parents. We visited the doctor for a medical assessment of our child, and not psychological assessments of us as parents. If we had needed psychological follow-up, we would have contacted a psychologist ourselves.

We also found it difficult that our concerns were linked to psychological conditions, when the child had already been referred to the health care system for medical assessment due to symptoms and family history that the GP was aware of. As parents, we therefore felt that our concerns had a natural background and should not be interpreted as a psychological problem on our part.

We experienced that some of the wording in the medical record did not correspond to what was said in the consultation. We were particularly upset by wording that we perceived as psychological assessments of us as parents, which we did not recognise and which we had not expressed. We also experienced that this was written by a doctor who did not know us, and who therefore had no basis for such advice or interpretations beyond what emerged in the consultation.

We also reacted to the fact that the medical record contained errors related to information we had provided during the consultation, which reinforced the feeling that we were not being properly listened to.

When we complained to Volvat, we did not feel that we were being accommodated when it came to having the section we reacted to the most removed, which we felt gave an incorrect and burdensome impression of us. We requested written justification from Volvat (complaints officer) several times for why the pediatrician would not change this, without receiving a response. The complaints process from Volvat was perceived as inadequate.

We later experienced that the content of the medical record influenced how we were met in further health services, when the record was commented on.

This is our personal experience, which we share because we do not want other parents to be in a similar situation.

I contacted them about a nut and gave them the part number. I asked several times if they were sure the part would fit my model year, and was confirmed three or four times that it would fit. The nut only cost 80 kroner, but I also paid 150 kroner in shipping, and they also wanted me to pay to send it back. It is difficult to understand how it can be reasonable for the customer to be left with all the costs when the dealer has repeatedly given incorrect information. In the end, the dealer ended up hanging up because he didn't want to spend time on it...🤠

There was so much nonsense here.
First, I am told during a tire change that both the brake discs and brake pads need to be replaced. When I ask if it is the front or rear brakes, they say "both". I have drum brakes in the back, which do not have brake discs and brake pads (so they clearly did not check the rear brakes).
When I still hand the car in for a brake change, I am told that the brakes are actually perfectly fine anyway, but they have now found out that my shock absorbers are leaking, so now they will be fixed instead. A series of delays follow, destruction of other parts during the repair, associated increased costs, and more delays. After that, the car makes a scraping noise when I turn. I go back so they can check the fault. They say it is because it is cold outside now. I go to another workshop, and they found the fault right away. In addition, they had not installed the reinforcement on the brake hose that goes through a mounting eye on the shock absorber, so over time it could have led to brake fluid leaks and defective brakes.
To be fair, my car has some rust, so some small parts that were broken during repairs are fair to happen, but the rest was just so incredibly sloppy.

My experience with this workshop was unfortunately not good, and I would not recommend it.

I ordered a service that was supposed to include an oil change and a 22-point inspection. In practice, I experienced that only an oil change was done. I was given a form with ticks, but these were filled out in front of me afterwards, which gives the impression that the inspection was not actually carried out thoroughly.

I know for myself that the brakes (discs/pads) are starting to wear out and make noise, and there are also signs of a leak from the gearbox. This was neither mentioned nor detected by the workshop.

Had today 28/04-26 general assembly regarding Peergyntveien 7, led by a SØBO representative in their premises.
I submitted a written response during the meeting, which was written by a lawyer chosen by Søbo, to a former chairman of the housing association that was relevant to the current window case, we have now had an ongoing disagreement for several years about who has the financial responsibility - the housing association or each individual resident.
As a Søbo lawyer concluded that EVERYTHING regarding the terraces, as well as the associated windows, rests with the housing association, except for daily cleaning/maintenance.
The meeting chairman from Søbo was, in my opinion, not very neutral, and was very reluctant to read this written statement out in the meeting, but after repeated demands and pressure from me, it was reluctantly read out---at a pace that was so fast that most people probably did not understand what was said.!!!!!
In my opinion, it was also a deliberate act, and absolutely worthy of criticism, and I got a nasty feeling that this was not very neutrally presented, as it was the only one of many writings that was treated like this.!!!!!
In addition, in my opinion, as well as several others, premises were rented for the shortest time possible, which was in my opinion also a deliberate act, to stress oneself at a high pace through unpleasant matters. To emphasize this, SØBO also said
The representative/chairman, ALREADY at the start of the meeting, that the premises were rented for far too short a time, and he might not be able to cover all matters, which substantiate what I write, and repeat themselves every year due to time constraints.
The representative knew this as it is the same person who chairs the meeting every year.
Such an attitude and tactic is not appropriate, as his job is to be neutral!!!!!
The meeting ended without all matters being addressed.!!!!!!! However, the person who was elected to approve that the general meeting had been completed was asked by the board 2/3 times, via text message, to approve the meeting as completed, but refused, so now, as the chairman himself stated at the start of the meeting, there must be another general meeting to complete all matters.!!!

The latest news is now that the person who was subjected to undue pressure, and finally could not resist, felt forced to sign.!!!!!
This is in my opinion a horror story on how a general meeting should NOT be carried out.!!!!!!!!
This is in my opinion neither legal nor a general meeting that is carried out according to the Housing Cooperatives Act.
The company needs to take an internal attitude check as this is not a company/representative I would recommend, the way this was handled.
In addition, the responsible BOARD LEADER should be aware of his responsibility, and call for a NEW general meeting and COMPLETE, but see it does not happen, which is highly deserving of criticism!!!
The Housing Cooperative Act states that a new general meeting can be required by 10% voting for this, which in our case is only 4 people.
If the general meeting is not carried out properly next year, it could easily be that this is the solution, or taken further through the right channels, but should be a step that should not be necessary, but time will tell.

Yours sincerely leif

It is completely voluntary to go to Telenor Arena. Yet, once again, I have done just that. I must be a complete idiot who voluntarily exposes myself to the torment of a soundscape that is completely devoid of character, dynamics and definition.

No matter how good the bands are, the sound often ends up as a diffuse mixture of bass, echo and noise. It is almost impossible to get the closeness and details in the music that the artists are actually trying to convey. The queues are endless, there are queues everywhere, and the smell of sweat, beer and poor ventilation lies like a heavy fog over the entire arena.

Yes, it is voluntary to go there. But it is also quite shameful that we in the capital of Norway still use a multi-purpose hall as a concert venue for some of the world's greatest artists. It feels both embarrassing and unambitious. We are one of the richest countries in the world, but when it comes to facilities for major concerts, it seems as if we have settled for "good enough".

And for the record: This is in no way a criticism of the artists. The band gave it their all and did a brilliant job. The problem is that the venue simply does not work for its purpose. Even the best musicians and sound engineers in the world cannot conjure up the fundamental challenges of an arena that was never designed to give the audience an optimal concert experience.

World-class artists deserve world-class settings. The audience deserves to hear the music as it is meant to be experienced. Until we take this seriously, Telenor Arena will continue to be a place people go to despite the arena – not because of it.

Rented a hot water pressure washer for a weekend project. Called in advance and got a clear answer that it was possible to rent over the weekend and pay for one day, since I picked up the machine just before closing time on Friday. The machine worked well, and I returned it Monday morning by 09:00, exactly as agreed.

The surprise came with the invoice – I was charged for two days of rental. It turns out that the small print in the contract states that the machines are equipped with GPS and record when they are in use. NKK is failing in its responsibility as a manager of national dog data when they choose to ignore documented facts. This creates a major safety risk for dogs in Norway, as the registry does not reflect actual living conditions or who has the responsibility for daily care. If you find yourself in a situation where legal ownership must be documented, you cannot "Expect help or legal understanding from NKK. Very unprofessional."

If it were possible to give this company 0 stars.
Stay far away from Mesterbedriften Lund. We chose them because of their slightly lower price than competing offers. Be careful. There is a reason why they are cheaper. Steer clear! Choose a competent master company instead. Our condominium used them to rehabilitate the stairs and replace the entrance doors to all of our sections. All the entrance doors had to be replaced as a result of improving fire safety and noise. Their painting work in our stairs was extremely fast and of very low quality, and it must be honestly said that I never saw anyone clean the walls before painting. Several points of defects and several rounds of correction from Lund were necessary. The worst thing was that they had not read the installation instructions for the fire doors/entrance doors and installed the doors incorrectly so that they were not fireproof. They installed them with fire foam while the installation instructions specified that Rockwool or similar should be used. It is disturbing that it was we on the board who noticed this and demanded rectification according to the installation instructions. The consequences could have been fatal if we had not noticed this - the possibility of non-fireproof doors or not receiving insurance settlement in the event of a fire as a result of the doors not being installed according to the installation instructions - i.e. not fireproof. Mesterbedriften Lund acknowledged that they had made a mistake and they started rectification of the entrance doors. In addition, when we asked about door pumps, we were told that they were not fire specialists, which they have proven. This was the start of a long, demanding and nightmarish process where they opened all the doors with crowbars, installed according to the installation instructions. In retrospect, there are visible traces of their rectification work that have not been corrected. We have also obtained a report from an objective third party who has commented on several shortcomings in their rectification work. Mesterbedriften Lund only refers to the fact that the defects we have commented on were reported too late and that they believe that there is no defect in the work performed and that the report is incorrect and that the assignment has been correctly performed and that they consider the matter closed on their part. Something that we and our legal advisor strongly disagree with. Lund commented that they have always installed doors in this way in many other assignments they have had and we are therefore concerned that there are many other fire doors in Oslo and the surrounding area that have not been installed correctly according to the installation instructions and are consequently not fireproof. There is a risk that such customers will not receive a settlement from the insurance company in the event of a fire. In addition, our experience is that the company mainly uses subcontractors who do not communicate in either English or Norwegian.

one_star_reviews.text:
I would like to express my disappointment with the experience we had with you today.

My boyfriend and I drove all the way from Lørenskog to Asker to visit your showroom to look at a sofa we are considering buying, as well as other models. On your website it says that the showroom is open until 6:00 PM, and we arrived around 4:50 PM. When we arrived, it was completely closed and no employees were present.

We called the Mobelia number, and the person we spoke to said that the showroom had to close earlier because a colleague had to go home. We understand that unforeseen things can happen, but at the same time it is very unprofessional and frustrating that this was not informed anywhere before we spent time and fuel traveling all the way to Asker.

In addition, your opening hours are very unclear and contradictory. On Google, there are different opening hours that do not match each other – including both 5:00 PM and 5:00 PM. 18:00 as closing time. Google also states that you are not open on Saturdays, while your website states that the showroom is open from 10:00–15:00 on Saturdays. This makes it difficult for customers to know what times actually apply.

When opening hours are listed publicly, one naturally expects them to be correct and that the showroom is available during these times. If employees have to leave earlier, in our opinion, a replacement should have been arranged or at least a notice should have been given on the website, Google or social media.

Unfortunately, this gave a bad impression, especially when we were considering shopping with you. We hope you take the feedback seriously so that other customers do not have to experience the same.
